title: The Rogue Council
summary: The unknown sender of calls to renewed struggle, also called the Sphinx.

claims.text: Soon after the Avatar Storm swallowed Horizon, an unknown sender began messaging mages across the world; it is called the Rogue Council or the Sphinx.
The messages favor no single Tradition and back no belief beyond a relentless pursuit of Ascension.
No one knows who or what the Rogue Council really is.
Messages come by many unpredictable routes: ordinary mail, email, or even radio and television broadcasts.
No Correspondence, Time or Forces magic has traced a message to its source, and none carries a Pattern signature, which hints at very powerful senders.
Most messages bear a sphinx emblem, seen on paper, as a shadow, as graffiti or in an advertisement; it fades away on the spot, though photographs of it stay clear.
Many messages are rousing calls to arms or accounts of wins and losses elsewhere in the struggle.

title: Tradition Reactions to the Rogue Council
summary: How the Traditions view the Sphinx's call.

claims.text: Many Tradition mages see the Rogue Council as a threat to the established order and its creed as a foolish call to consequence-free anarchy.
Others read its message as a call to Ascension that draws on the views of every Tradition at once.
After the Avatar Storm, some mages took the turmoil as proof that either the Technocracy had won or humanity had stopped caring.

title: Panopticon
summary: A cross-Convention Technocratic Methodology formed to hunt the Rogue Council's followers.

claims.text: Panopticon formed less than a month after the first transmissions but took about six months to win the respect of Earth-based amalgams and Constructs.
It uses military ranks and draws soldiers from Iteration X BioMechanics, NWO Operatives, Progenitor Damage Control and the Void Engineer Border Corps.
It is standardizing field gear and codes across the Conventions and has brought HIT Marks back into use.
